pr.title: Make `ConstPropLint` lint run on promoteds
pr.description:
Fixes #117949 wherein the lint didn't fire for the following promoteds:

- SHL or SHR operators in a non-optimized build
- any arithmetic operator in an optimized build

What I have done here is simply enabled `ConstPropLint` to run on promoted bodies by removing the relevant `if` check.

After this change _all_ promoted arithmetic operators will lint _in both non-optimized and optimized builds_. On the flip side programs containing the above mentioned overflowing promoteds that were accepted earlier will now be rejected. Hope that is okay from a backward compatibility standpoint.

I have added tests covering all overflowing promoted & non-promoted ops for both compile-time and runtime operations and for optimized as well as non-optimized builds.

I had to amend some existing tests to make them pass and had to delete a couple that were set to pass despite overflows.

This PR increases the number of duplicate diagnostics emitted (because the same operator might get linted in both the promoted MIR and the main MIR). I hope that is an acceptable trade-off given that we now lint overflows much more comprehensively than earlier.
pr.author: gurry

issues.title: arithmetic_overflow lint not triggered for overflowing shifts in promoteds
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

### I tried this code:

```rust
format_args!("{}", 1 << 32)
```

### I expected to see this happen:

Same output as
```rust
let a = 1 << 32;
format_args!("{}", a)
```
which would be
```
error: this arithmetic operation will overflow
 --> src/main.rs:3:9
  |
3 | let a = 1 << 32;
  |         ^^^^^^^ attempt to shift left by `32_i32`, which would overflow
  |
  = note: `#[deny(arithmetic_overflow)]` on by default
```

### Instead, this happened:

The code compiles with no error, the lint is not produced.
When running it, it overflows: panics at debug mode, and gives the wrong output in release.

### Meta
<!--
If you're using the stable version of the compiler, you should also check if the
bug also exists in the beta or nightly versions.
-->

Tested with the current stable, nightly and beta from the playground.

I have tried finding whether this has already been reported, it seems it hasn't

analysis.originalLogic: `ConstPropLint` (compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/const_prop_lint.rs) intentionally skipped promoted MIR bodies before doing any lint work. The pre-fix body contained an early return guarded by the promoted source check, with the rationale that promoteds were expected to be evaluated by Miri: the patch removes exactly `// will be evaluated by miri and produce its errors there` followed by `if body.source.promoted.is_some() { return; }`. Consequently the lint only ran on the main function MIR, not on the synthetic promoted bodies that hold const-promoted expressions such as borrowed temporaries and `format_args!` arguments.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation/behavior was the early-return filter: whenever a MIR body came from a promotion (`body.source.promoted.is_some()`), `ConstPropLint` returned without linting. As the PR states, this caused the lint not to fire for `SHL or SHR operators in a non-optimized build` and `any arithmetic operator in an optimized build`. Thus an overflowing operation placed inside a promoted body (for example `let _n = &(1u8 << 8);` or `format_args!("{}", 1 << 32)`) was silently accepted instead of producing the same arithmetic-overflow diagnostic as the non-promoted form. The corrected behavior removes that promoted-body early return so promoted MIR is linted too.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR bodies that include const promotions: expressions whose value is borrowed/promoted, e.g. `&(EXPR)` and operands inside `format_args!`. The relevant EXPRs are integer arithmetic and bounds operations: left/right shifts by the bit width or more, add/sub/mul that overflow, division/remainder by zero, and out-of-bounds array indexing, across signed/unsigned integer types including `isize`/`usize`. Relevant build configurations are non-optimized (`-C opt-level=0`), optimized (`-O`), and optimized with runtime overflow checks (`-C overflow-checks=on -O`). The same source expressions may appear both non-promoted (`let _n = EXPR;`) and promoted (`let _n = &(EXPR);`), and const-item contexts use const evaluation errors rather than the runtime lint.
analysis.summary: Bug-fix PR enabling `ConstPropLint` to lint promoted MIR bodies. Previously the pass returned early for `body.source.promoted.is_some()`, so overflowing arithmetic inside promoted expressions (e.g. `format_args!("{}", 1 << 32)` or `&(1u8 << 8)`) escaped the arithmetic-overflow/unconditional-panic lints. Removing the promoted guard makes promoted and non-promoted forms lint consistently across no-opt, optimized, and overflow-checked builds, at the cost of duplicate diagnostics when the same operator is linted in both promoted and main MIR.
analysis.trigger: An expression is const-promoted (a borrowed temporary such as `&(1u8 << 8)` or a `format_args!` argument such as `1 << 32`) and the operation overflows, shifts by at least the bit width, divides/remainders by zero, or indexes out of bounds. Before the fix, `ConstPropLint` skipped promoted bodies and emitted no diagnostic; after the fix it lints the promoted operation in both non-optimized and optimized builds.
preconditions: The MIR body being linted has a promoted source (`body.source.promoted.is_some()`), i.e. the operation lives in a const-promoted expression rather than only in the main MIR.

The operation is an arithmetic/overflow operation covered by the lint (shift, add, sub, mul, div, rem) or a bounds operation such as out-of-bounds indexing that produces an unconditional-panic diagnostic.

The arithmetic_overflow lint is enabled/denied (it is deny-by-default as noted in the test stderr: `#[deny(arithmetic_overflow)]` on by default), and the operation is not instead handled as a hard const-eval error.
The promoted body is actually reached by the lint pipeline; the fix removes the promoted-source early return (`if body.source.promoted.is_some() { return; }`) that previously prevented this.
pitfalls: Removing the promoted guard increases duplicate diagnostics: the PR states `This PR increases the number of duplicate diagnostics emitted (because the same operator might get linted in both the promoted MIR and the main MIR).` Tests account for this with `-Z deduplicate-diagnostics=yes` and stderr notes such as `duplicate diagnostic emitted due to -Z deduplicate-diagnostics=no`.
Optimization level changes which promotions/paths are linted, so a single non-revision test is insufficient; the regression test uses revisions `noopt`, `opt`, and `opt_with_overflow_checks`.

The fix intentionally changes acceptance: the PR warns that `programs containing the above mentioned overflowing promoteds that were accepted earlier will now be rejected`, so old tests that asserted passing behavior for overflowing promoteds had to be removed or amended (e.g. deleting `promoted_overflow_opt.rs`).

Do not confuse const-item evaluation errors (`error[E0080]: evaluation of constant value failed`) with the codegen-time lint (`this arithmetic operation will overflow` / `this operation will panic at runtime`); the new `overflowing-consts.rs` covers the former and `lint-overflowing-ops.rs` the latter.
Pointer-width-dependent shift counts require normalization (`shift left by (64|32)_usize` -> `%BITS%`) so the test works on 32-bit and 64-bit targets.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test with revisions `noopt` (`-C opt-level=0`), `opt` (`-O`), and `opt_with_overflow_checks` (`-C overflow-checks=on -O`), using `-Z deduplicate-diagnostics=yes` to normalize the newly increased duplicate diagnostics. Include the exact issue reproducer `format_args!("{}", 1 << 32)` as well as shifted-right, add, sub, mul, div-by-zero, rem-by-zero, and `[1, 2, 3][4]` promoted operands. To probe the transformation directly, pair each promoted form with its non-promoted twin, e.g. `let _n = 1u8 << 8;` and `let _n = &(1u8 << 8);`, and assert both emit `arithmetic operation will overflow` (or `this operation will panic at runtime` for div/rem/OOB). Cover every signed/unsigned integer width and `isize`/`usize`, normalize `%BITS%` for pointer-width shifts, and keep a separate const-item suite for E0080 errors. Treat all test changes as expected-output updates, not as evidence that a compiler was built or that the bug was reproduced here.
